content: Vaginal bleeding or breast enlargement may occur as side effects of this medication. These symptoms typically resolve within the first month of treatment. If they persist beyond two months, it may indicate non-compliance with the treatment regimen or the presence of gonadotropin-independent sexual precocity. If these possibilities are ruled out, the dosage may be increased to 1800 mcg per day, administered as 600 mcg three times daily. Patients experiencing nasal conditions, such as rhinitis, should consult their physician before using topical nasal decongestants. If a decongestant is necessary during treatment, it should not be used until at least two hours after administering the medication. Sneezing during or immediately after administration should be avoided, as it may impair drug absorption. Seizures have been reported in patients receiving GnRH agonists, including those with a history of seizures, epilepsy, cerebrovascular disorders, central nervous system anomalies or tumors, or those taking medications associated with seizures, such as bupropion and SSRIs. Seizures have also been reported in patients without any of these conditions. Psychiatric events, including emotional lability (e.g., crying, irritability, impatience, anger, and aggression), have been reported in patients using GnRH agonists. Patients should be monitored for the development or worsening of psychiatric symptoms during treatment. Depression may occur or worsen during therapy, particularly in individuals with a history of depression. Women with new or worsening depression should be referred to a mental health professional as appropriate. Patients should be informed about the potential for depression and advised to report concerning thoughts or behaviors to their healthcare provider immediately. Pseudotumor cerebri (idiopathic intracranial hypertension) has been reported in pediatric patients receiving GnRH agonists, including nafarelin acetate. Patients should be monitored for symptoms such as headache, papilledema, blurred vision, double vision, vision loss, pain behind the eyes or with eye movement, tinnitus, dizziness, and nausea. Patients and caregivers should be informed about the possibility of pseudotumor cerebri. This medication is classified as Pregnancy Category X and is contraindicated during pregnancy due to the potential for harm to an unborn baby. Its excretion in breast milk is unknown, and breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Nafarelin is a synthetic decapeptide that acts as a GnRH agonist, desensitizing the response to endogenous GnRH, which reduces the secretion of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), subsequently decreasing ovarian and testicular hormone production. The medication reaches peak serum levels within 10 to 45 minutes, with a half-life of approximately 3 hours. It is metabolized by peptidase enzymes and excreted through urine (44-55%) and feces (19-44%). Its bioavailability is low (1-6%). The onset of its initial effect occurs within one month, with peak effects for endometriosis observed at 12 weeks. Nafarelin is used in women to treat endometriosis, a condition where uterine lining tissue grows outside the uterus. It is also used in children to treat central precocious puberty (gonadotropin-dependent early puberty). Nafarelin mimics the natural hormone gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) produced by the body. To use this medication, read the provided Medication Guide and follow the illustrated instructions carefully. If using a new bottle, perform test sprays into the air as directed. Gently blow your nose before use. Administer the medication as prescribed, typically twice daily (approximately every 12 hours). If more than one spray is required, wait 30 seconds between sprays. Avoid spraying the medication into your eyes and sneezing during or immediately after use, as this may reduce absorption. Follow the cleaning instructions for the spray tip. It is crucial to use the medication exactly as prescribed and not to skip doses. Do not use the nasal spray bottle beyond its recommended duration, even if medication remains, as the full dose may not be delivered. When starting this medication, symptoms may temporarily worsen, such as increased vaginal bleeding in women treating endometriosis or signs of puberty (e.g., breast enlargement, pubic hair growth, oily skin, or body odor) in children treating early puberty. These symptoms should improve after the first month of treatment. Common side effects in children include nasal irritation, hot flashes, or vaginal discharge. In women, side effects may include nasal irritation, hot flashes, headaches, decreased sexual interest, muscle pain, vaginal dryness, acne, or reduced breast size. Serious allergic reactions are rare but possible. If you experience severe symptoms, seek medical attention immediately. Before using nafarelin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, GnRH, or similar hormones (e.g., leuprolide), or if you have other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Discuss the use of non-hormonal birth control methods (e.g., condoms, diaphragms with spermicide) with your doctor, as this medication is not a reliable form of contraception. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication due to potential risks to the infant. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false results. If an overdose occurs, seek emergency medical attention or contact a poison control center immediately. Regular lab and medical tests (e.g., growth and bone age velocity in children) should be conducted during treatment. Store the medication upright at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not freeze or store it in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
